name: Anak
description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: They returned after forty days and agreed the land flowed with milk and honey; then verse 28 turns on one word: nevertheless. The people be strong, the cities are walled, we saw the children of Anak. Doubt entered on the heels of the promise.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: They returned and reported the land floweth with milk and honey, and showed the fruit; nevertheless the people be strong, the cities walled and very great, and the children of Anak were there. Caleb stilled the people and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

points: The spies had discouraged their hearts with the report: the people greater and taller than we, cities great and walled up to heaven, and the sons of the Anakims, the giants, in the land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

points: The Emims dwelt in that land in times past, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims, accounted giants; and the Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, and the children of Esau succeeded them and dwelt in their stead.

note.label: Deuteronomy 2: Meddle Not With Them, and the Giants That Perished

points: Ammon's land was also accounted a land of giants: the Zamzummims, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims; and the Lord destroyed them, and the Ammonites succeeded them and dwelt in their stead.

note.label: Deuteronomy 2: Meddle Not With Them, and the Giants That Perished

points: At that time came Joshua and cut off the Anakims from the mountains, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah and Israel; Joshua destroyed them utterly with their cities. None of the Anakims were left in the land of the children of Israel: only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod there remained.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: At that time Joshua cut off the Anakims from the mountains: the Anakims are the giants. He was fighting giants. None were left in the land of the children of Israel: only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod there remained. That is where Goliath the Philistine came from later.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Caleb asks for the very mountain the Anakims were in: now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day, for thou heardest how the Anakims were there and the cities were great and fenced; if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

points: The name of Hebron before was Kirjatharba, which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

points: Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.

note.label: Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah

points: They received Hebron in the hill country of Judah, the city of Arba the father of Anak, to be a city of refuge for the slayer; but the fields and villages of the city belonged to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: Hebron is given unto Caleb, as Moses said, and he expels thence the three sons of Anak.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out
